title: GMAT Quant: Problem Solving (No Data Sufficiency Here)
summary: GMAT Focus Quant is now pure Problem Solving — 21 questions of algebra and arithmetic reasoning, no geometry-heavy tricks, no calculator.

nodes.label: Algebra & arithmetic

chunks.heading: One question type: Problem Solving
chunks.body: GMAT Focus Quant is **only Problem Solving** — standard five-option multiple-choice maths questions. **Data Sufficiency has moved to the Data Insights section**, so Quant is now a cleaner, single-format section of **21 questions in 45 minutes**.
chunks.realExample: If you prepped from old GMAT material expecting Data Sufficiency in Quant, drop it here — you'll meet DS in Data Insights instead. Quant is pure 'solve and pick the answer'.
chunks.memoryHook: Quant = Problem Solving only. Data Sufficiency lives in Data Insights now.

chunks.heading: It's reasoning, not heavy computation
chunks.body: Content is **algebra and arithmetic** — word problems, ratios, percentages, number properties, basic statistics. There's **no on-screen calculator in Quant**, so the test rewards **smart setup and estimation**, not brute-force calculation.
chunks.realExample: Instead of computing 17% of 350 exactly, estimate: 10% is 35, plus half again ≈ 52.5. Fast estimation often eliminates enough options to answer without exact arithmetic.
chunks.memoryHook: No calculator = they want reasoning, not arithmetic. Estimate and eliminate.

chunks.heading: Plug in and back-solve
chunks.body: Two reliable tactics: **plug in numbers** for variable-heavy questions, and **back-solve** by testing the answer choices (start with the middle value). These turn abstract algebra into concrete arithmetic you can check.
chunks.realExample: For 'if the answer choices are 10, 20, 30, 40, 50', test 30 first: too big or small tells you which way to jump, so you rarely test more than two choices.
chunks.memoryHook: Stuck on algebra? Plug in real numbers or back-solve from the middle choice.

chunks.heading: Pace and don't stall
chunks.body: About **2 minutes per question**. Because it's **adaptive**, an early stumble matters — but so does finishing, so **don't sink five minutes into one question**. Bookmark a monster, make your best guess, and use the review screen if time allows.
chunks.realExample: Two minutes in with no path forward? Eliminate what you can, guess, bookmark, and move — one skipped-but-guessed question costs far less than three rushed ones at the end.
chunks.memoryHook: ~2 min each. Never let one question eat five. Guess, bookmark, move.

recall.q: What question type does GMAT Focus Quant contain?
recall.a: Only Problem Solving — Data Sufficiency has moved to the Data Insights section.

recall.q: How many questions and minutes is the Quant section?
Is a calculator allowed in GMAT Quant?
recall.a: No — Quant has no on-screen calculator, so it rewards smart setup and estimation.

recall.q: What are two reliable tactics for hard Quant questions?
recall.a: Plugging in real numbers for variables, and back-solving by testing the answer choices from the middle.

recall.q: What should you do when stuck on a Quant question?
recall.a: Eliminate what you can, guess, bookmark it, and move on — don't let one question eat several minutes.
